title: What a Heritage Day Can Begin
source_title: Nationwide intangible cultural heritage promotion initiative launched in Beijing
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开信息；本站依据有限事实重新确定中心问题、重组结构并原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
A special day can bring traditional skills into public view, but one day is only a beginning. Around China's Cultural and Natural Heritage Day in 2024, a nationwide program planned more than 12,000 activities. At the China Intangible Cultural Heritage Museum in Beijing, five inheritors gave works to the museum. A year-long exhibition also opened there.

The exhibition presented more than 100 heritage projects, from local opera materials to embroidery and wood carving. More than 600 pieces or sets were shown through displays that included multimedia. These numbers describe a wide doorway into living culture. They do not, however, tell us whether a visitor will later learn a craft, attend an opera, or understand why a practice matters to its community.

Promotion therefore has two jobs. First, it must make traditions visible and approachable. Second, it should create a path from looking to continued interest. A short label may identify an object, while a demonstration can reveal the decisions and practice behind it. A museum program can also direct visitors toward local groups and future events.

The useful question after Heritage Day is not simply how many people came. It is whether the encounter gave them a reason and a way to return.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why heritage promotion should connect public attention with later engagement
Why museums should replace all local festivals
How to count every traditional object in China
Why multimedia should be removed from exhibitions
questions.explanation: 文章先介绍推广活动，再强调真正的问题是能否把一次参观转化为持续参与。
questions.evidence_text: Promotion therefore has two jobs. First, it must make traditions visible and approachable. Second, it should create a path from looking to continued interest.

questions.question: What happened at the museum in Beijing?
options: It closed its year-long exhibition
Five inheritors donated works
It trained 12,000 new performers
It displayed only wood carving
questions.explanation: 首段明确说五位传承人向博物馆捐赠了作品。
questions.evidence_text: At the China Intangible Cultural Heritage Museum in Beijing, five inheritors gave works to the museum.

questions.question: What does “approachable” most nearly mean in paragraph 3?
options: Easy for the public to enter and understand
Too valuable to be displayed
Unchanged for hundreds of years
Known only to trained artists
questions.explanation: 该词与 visible 并列，并与让公众从观看走向兴趣的语境相连，指容易接近和理解。
questions.evidence_text: First, it must make traditions visible and approachable.

questions.question: Why does the author mention demonstrations?
options: To show that objects should never be labeled
To suggest that seeing a process can deepen understanding
To prove that opera is easier than embroidery
To argue that every visitor must become an inheritor
questions.explanation: 由“展示技艺背后的选择与练习”可推断，过程展示比只看物件更有助于深入理解。
questions.evidence_text: A short label may identify an object, while a demonstration can reveal the decisions and practice behind it.

options: Useful as a starting point but insufficient by themselves

Successful only when attendance is free
Unnecessary once objects enter a museum
questions.explanation: 开头明确肯定活动带来关注，同时限定“一天只是开始”。
questions.evidence_text: A special day can bring traditional skills into public view, but one day is only a beginning.

title: A Tradition Large Enough to Need Coordination
source_title: Qintong Boat Festival held in Taizhou, E China
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网图片报道的标题与图注事实；本站原创改写，不补造图注之外的历史细节，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
From the air, the 2025 Qintong Boat Festival looked like a great gathering on water. More than 500 boats and over 10,000 boat-team members met at Qinhu National Wetland Park in Taizhou. Performers moved across the water while crowds watched from nearby. The event belongs to a centuries-old tradition and entered China's national intangible cultural heritage list in 2008.

Scale gives the festival energy, yet it also changes the work required to keep the tradition alive. A small local practice can depend on personal knowledge and informal arrangements. A gathering of thousands needs routes, timing, safety rules, and cooperation between teams. These practical systems are not separate from culture. They allow participants to perform together without turning the event into disorder.

Large public attention creates another challenge. Spectators may remember the impressive number of boats but miss the skills, relationships, and preparation that make the gathering possible. Organizers can address this by explaining how teams prepare and why the water setting matters. Such information does not reduce the excitement; it gives the scene a human scale.

The festival therefore shows two forms of continuity. One is official recognition, which records the tradition's importance. The other is renewed coordination among living participants. A heritage label can protect a name, but only people can organize the next meeting on the water.

questions.question: How large was the gathering described in the passage?
options: About 50 boats and 1,000 members
More than 500 boats and over 10,000 members
Exactly 200 boats and 8,000 members
Fewer than 100 boats and 500 members
questions.explanation: 首段直接给出船只和队员数量。
questions.evidence_text: More than 500 boats and over 10,000 boat-team members met at Qinhu National Wetland Park in Taizhou.

questions.question: What central point does the author make about the festival?
options: Its survival depends on both recognition and active organization
Its value comes entirely from its size

Its water setting is no longer important
questions.explanation: 全文对比官方认定与参与者持续组织，指出两者共同维持传统。
questions.evidence_text: The festival therefore shows two forms of continuity.

questions.question: What does “informal” most nearly mean in paragraph 2?
options: Not based on official procedures
Open only to tourists

questions.explanation: 该词与 personal knowledge 并列，并与大活动需要正式路线和规则形成对照。
questions.evidence_text: A small local practice can depend on personal knowledge and informal arrangements.

questions.question: Why should organizers explain how teams prepare?
options: To help spectators see more than a striking visual scene
To persuade teams to use fewer boats
To replace performances with lectures

questions.explanation: 前文说观众可能只记住船多，解释准备过程能让他们理解背后的技能与关系。
questions.evidence_text: Spectators may remember the impressive number of boats but miss the skills, relationships, and preparation that make the gathering possible.

options: It weakens cultural meaning

questions.explanation: 作者认为路线、安全和协作不是文化之外的负担，而是共同表演得以实现的条件。
questions.evidence_text: These practical systems are not separate from culture.

title: When Technology Performs Tradition
source_title: 21st China (Shenzhen) Int'l Cultural Industries Fair kicks off
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网图片报道的标题与图注事实；本站围绕技术展示与文化理解的张力原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
At a cultural industries fair in Shenzhen, visitors could encounter tradition through several kinds of technology. Robots performed the energetic Yingge dance, another robot played the guzheng, and a virtual-reality experience offered a tour of Dunhuang. Elsewhere, live performers presented intangible heritage, while models, archives, and creative products filled exhibition areas. The fair ran from May 22 to 26, 2025.

These scenes raise a question that a busy exhibition may leave unanswered: when technology performs culture, what exactly is being communicated? A robot can repeat a movement with striking precision, and virtual reality can place distant images around a visitor. Both may attract someone who would otherwise walk past. Attention is valuable because learning cannot begin without it.

Yet a technically impressive display can also flatten differences. Yingge is not simply a set of rapid actions, just as the guzheng is more than the notes produced by its strings. Human practices contain decisions about occasion, training, interpretation, and relationships among performers. If a machine presents only the visible surface, viewers may mistake accurate imitation for complete understanding.

The answer is not to keep new tools away from old culture. Curators can use a robot performance as an opening question, then connect it with human accounts, historical context, and live practice. A VR tour can clarify distance and space while still directing attention to the people who study and protect a site.

Technology is most useful here as a bridge rather than a substitute. Its success should be measured not only by the crowd it gathers, but by whether visitors leave curious about the living knowledge behind the spectacle.

questions.question: Which experience at the fair was linked to Dunhuang?
options: A boat performance
A virtual-reality tour
An embroidery contest
A wetland walk
questions.explanation: 首段说明虚拟现实体验提供了敦煌之旅。
questions.evidence_text: a virtual-reality experience offered a tour of Dunhuang.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly arguing?
options: Technology should replace live cultural practice
Cultural fairs should display only machines

questions.explanation: 文章既肯定技术吸引注意，也强调需要人的讲述和历史语境来避免表层模仿。
questions.evidence_text: Technology is most useful here as a bridge rather than a substitute.

questions.question: What does “flatten” mean in paragraph 3?
options: Make important differences seem unimportant
Increase the physical height of a display
Translate a performance into another language
Prevent visitors from entering an exhibition
questions.explanation: 下文说明机器可能只呈现可见表面，因此 flatten 指抹平或忽略文化实践中的差异。
questions.evidence_text: Yet a technically impressive display can also flatten differences.

questions.question: Why does the author call attention valuable?
options: It guarantees complete cultural knowledge
It creates an opportunity for further learning

questions.explanation: 作者明确说没有注意就无法开始学习，因此注意力是进一步理解的入口而非终点。
questions.evidence_text: Attention is valuable because learning cannot begin without it.

options: Showing a robot without any explanation

questions.explanation: 第四段直接建议以机器表演为开端，再连接人的讲述、历史背景和现场实践。
questions.evidence_text: Curators can use a robot performance as an opening question, then connect it with human accounts, historical context, and live practice.

title: How Three Hundred Objects Become One Exhibition
source_title: Shanghai Museum East to hold exhibition on Hongshan culture
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网图片报道的标题与图注事实；本站围绕跨机构展览叙事原创改写，未扩写来源未载的具体文物结论，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
An exhibition on Hongshan culture at Shanghai Museum East brought together more than 300 cultural objects from twenty museums and archaeological institutions. Due to open on June 26, 2025, it used dragon imagery to introduce an ancient civilization. The culture represented by the exhibition dates to roughly 5,000–6,000 years ago.

Such figures signal breadth, but they also reveal a curatorial problem. Objects gathered from many collections do not automatically form an explanation. Each institution may have classified, stored, or displayed its material within a different local history. Once the pieces enter a shared gallery, visitors need to understand why these particular objects have been placed together and what claims the arrangement can reasonably support.

One solution is to treat sequence as an argument. An opening group might introduce the environment and time period; later sections could compare forms, uses, or places of discovery. Labels should identify uncertainty as carefully as they identify accepted knowledge. When archaeologists disagree about an object's function, hiding that disagreement may make the exhibition sound confident, but it removes an important part of how knowledge is built.

Collaboration among twenty institutions can strengthen this approach. No single collection needs to stand for the whole culture, and objects separated by modern ownership can be compared in one space. At the same time, institutional scale is not proof of a single interpretation. More lenders can expand the evidence without eliminating debate.

The exhibition's real achievement, then, cannot be counted only in objects. A successful gallery makes a large collection legible: visitors should see both the patterns that connect the material and the gaps that keep interpretation open. Curating prehistory is not the act of filling every silence. It is the disciplined work of showing how much the surviving evidence permits us to say.

questions.question: What did the exhibition bring together?
options: Over 300 objects from twenty institutions
Twenty objects from 300 private owners
Only digital copies from one museum
Objects made during the year 2025
questions.explanation: 首段直接说明展品数量与参与机构数量。
questions.evidence_text: An exhibition on Hongshan culture at Shanghai Museum East brought together more than 300 cultural objects from twenty museums and archaeological institutions.

questions.question: Why might hiding scholarly disagreement be harmful?
options: It makes objects physically harder to protect
It prevents visitors from seeing how interpretations are formed
It forces institutions to return their loans
It reduces the total number of labels
questions.explanation: 作者认为分歧本身体现知识如何建立，隐藏分歧会制造虚假的确定性。
questions.evidence_text: hiding that disagreement may make the exhibition sound confident, but it removes an important part of how knowledge is built.

questions.question: What does “legible” most nearly mean in the final paragraph?
options: Easy to understand as an organized account
Written in several ancient languages
Protected from all disagreement
Owned by a single institution
questions.explanation: 冒号后的解释要求观众看见材料间的联系与空白，因此 legible 指组织清楚、可理解。
questions.evidence_text: A successful gallery makes a large collection legible

questions.question: Which statement best expresses the author's main argument?
options: A large archaeological exhibition needs a transparent argument, not merely many objects
Every prehistoric object has one certain meaning
Museums should avoid borrowing from other institutions
Visitor numbers are the best measure of scholarship
questions.explanation: 全文围绕如何把多机构、多展品组织成有边界且承认不确定性的解释。
questions.evidence_text: Objects gathered from many collections do not automatically form an explanation.

questions.question: How does the author view cross-institutional collaboration?
options: Valuable for widening evidence, though it cannot settle every debate
Useful only for lowering ticket prices
Likely to destroy local histories
Unnecessary when an exhibition has a strong title
questions.explanation: 作者肯定合作扩大证据，又明确说机构规模并不能证明只有一种解释。
questions.evidence_text: More lenders can expand the evidence without eliminating debate.

title: Who Carries a Festival Forward?
source_title: Miao Sisters Festival kicks off in Taijiang, SW China
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网图片报道的标题与图注事实；本站围绕节庆参与和公共呈现原创改写，不把图像中的单次活动泛化为完整传统史，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Photographs from Taijiang County in Guizhou show the Miao Sisters Festival as a public event with many kinds of participation. In April 2024, adults and children joined a parade; women prepared silver jewelry, an embroidery competition took place, and one participant carried “sisters' rice” with an egg. A dragon dance also formed part of the celebration. The festival, recognized as national intangible cultural heritage, was scheduled to continue until May 5 that year.

A photographic record is powerful because it captures detail: the weight and shine of jewelry, the concentration before a competition, or different generations moving through the same street. Yet a photograph also selects. It preserves one instant and one viewpoint, while the preparation before the shutter and the meanings understood by participants remain outside the frame. Public images should therefore be treated as invitations to inquiry, not as complete definitions of a tradition.

This matters when festivals attract audiences beyond their home community. Visibility can support recognition and create opportunities for local makers and performers. However, if publicity repeatedly favors the most colorful scene, quieter forms of knowledge may become harder to notice. The person who teaches embroidery, organizes a family's clothing, or explains when an object should be used may contribute as much to continuity as the performer at the center of a photograph.

Documentation can respond to this imbalance without trying to record everything. Organizers might pair event images with short accounts from participants of different ages and roles. They can distinguish what a photograph directly shows from what an interviewee explains. That practice preserves the value of visual evidence while preventing the image from claiming more than it knows.

The question “Who carries a festival forward?” therefore has no single dramatic answer. Continuity is distributed across visible performance, routine teaching, material preparation, and the choices a community makes about public presentation. Recognition is meaningful, but heritage remains living only when people can shape how it is practiced and represented.

questions.question: Which activity is directly reported in the passage?
options: A national boat race
An embroidery competition
A virtual tour of Dunhuang
A museum donation ceremony
questions.explanation: 首段列举了刺绣比赛这一现场活动。
questions.evidence_text: an embroidery competition took place

questions.question: Why does the author describe a photograph as an invitation to inquiry?
options: Because it offers useful detail but leaves context outside the frame
Because photographs contain no reliable information

questions.explanation: 第二段先肯定图像细节，再指出准备过程与参与者理解不在画面内，因此图像应引出进一步追问。
questions.evidence_text: It preserves one instant and one viewpoint, while the preparation before the shutter and the meanings understood by participants remain outside the frame.

questions.question: What central issue does the passage examine?
options: How public images can represent a festival without defining it completely
Why festivals should no longer be photographed

questions.explanation: 全文讨论照片带来的可见性及其选择性，并提出补充参与者讲述的做法。
questions.evidence_text: Public images should therefore be treated as invitations to inquiry, not as complete definitions of a tradition.

questions.question: What may happen if publicity focuses mainly on colorful scenes?

questions.explanation: 作者把高可见场景与较安静的传承劳动对照，可推断后者可能被忽视。
questions.evidence_text: if publicity repeatedly favors the most colorful scene, quieter forms of knowledge may become harder to notice.

questions.question: Which documentation practice does the author support?
options: Presenting one striking photograph as the whole tradition
Pairing images with accounts from people in different roles
Recording only professional performers
Removing all interpretation from public displays
questions.explanation: 第四段明确建议将活动图像与不同年龄、角色参与者的简短讲述配对。
questions.evidence_text: Organizers might pair event images with short accounts from participants of different ages and roles.

title: Why a Carbon Plan Needs More Than One Lever
source_title: Full text: Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality China's Plans and Solutions
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开白皮书报道；本站只选取有限数字与政策关系，重新组织并原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Cutting carbon is sometimes described as one simple task: replace an old energy source with a cleaner one. In practice, a national transition has many connected parts. A 2025 white paper described China's approach as balancing growth with lower emissions, long-term goals with near-term action, and government direction with market activity.

Energy change is central. The share of non-fossil energy in consumption rose from 16.0 percent in 2020 to 19.8 percent in 2024. During the same period, the fossil-energy share fell from 84.0 percent to 80.2 percent. But new supply alone cannot complete the job. Power networks must connect generation, demand, and storage reliably.

Other sectors also matter. Factories can improve efficiency, transport can use lower-carbon equipment, and buildings can reduce waste. A circular economy keeps materials in use, while healthy ecosystems can store carbon. These actions work at different points: some prevent emissions, some reduce the resources needed, and others remove carbon from the air.

That is why climate policy needs several levers. A single successful project may be useful, but it cannot represent the whole transition. Progress depends on whether energy, industry, daily life, and natural systems move in a compatible direction.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Carbon reduction requires coordinated action across several systems
Only household choices can lower emissions
Fossil energy disappeared by 2024
Storage is the only climate solution
questions.explanation: 全文列举能源、产业、生活和生态系统，强调多种手段需要协同。
questions.evidence_text: That is why climate policy needs several levers.

questions.question: What happened to the non-fossil energy share from 2020 to 2024?
options: It rose from 16.0 percent to 19.8 percent
It fell from 19.8 percent to 16.0 percent
It stayed at 80.2 percent
It reached 100 percent
questions.explanation: 第二段直接给出了2020年和2024年的比例。
questions.evidence_text: The share of non-fossil energy in consumption rose from 16.0 percent in 2020 to 19.8 percent in 2024.

questions.question: What does “levers” mean in the final paragraph?
options: Different tools for producing change
Machines used only in factories
Numbers that cannot be compared
Rules for closing power networks
questions.explanation: 前文列举多种减排手段，levers 在此比喻可推动变化的不同工具。
questions.evidence_text: That is why climate policy needs several levers.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention power networks?
options: To show that cleaner generation must be integrated into a reliable system
To argue that energy demand should be ignored
To prove that storage increases fossil use
To suggest that factories should manage all electricity
questions.explanation: 作者在新能源比例后补充电网、需求和储能，说明只有新增清洁供给仍不够。
questions.evidence_text: Power networks must connect generation, demand, and storage reliably.

questions.question: How does the author view a single successful climate project?
options: Useful but not a complete picture of transition
Enough to represent all national progress
Less important than avoiding measurement
Proof that other sectors need no change
questions.explanation: 末段明确限定单个项目有用，却不能代表整个转型。
questions.evidence_text: A single successful project may be useful, but it cannot represent the whole transition.

title: Reopening a Wetland Without Closing the Question
source_title: Haiwei National Wetland Park in China's Hainan reopens to public after ecological restoration
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网图片报道的标题与图注事实；本站围绕开放与持续监测的关系原创改写，不补造未公开的修复技术细节，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Haiwei National Wetland Park in Hainan reopened to visitors after ecological restoration and the construction of public facilities. The park is an important stop for migratory birds, and recent protection and monitoring recorded 213 bird species. The reopening might look like the final step of a completed project. Ecologically, however, it is better understood as the start of a new test.

Before visitors return, managers can control many activities inside a site. Reopening changes that situation. Foot traffic, noise, litter, and movement near feeding or resting areas may create pressures that were limited during restoration. Facilities can guide people, but their location and use must be observed in real conditions.

The count of 213 species provides a useful baseline, a starting measure for later comparison. It should not be treated as a permanent score. Migratory birds do not appear in the same numbers every month, and a change in a count can have more than one cause. Managers therefore need repeated observations across seasons, together with records of visitor activity and habitat conditions.

Public access can also support protection. Visitors who understand why paths have boundaries are more likely to respect them, and careful viewing can build interest in the wetland. The aim is not to choose between people and birds. It is to design access that can be adjusted when evidence shows stress. A reopened gate marks progress, but responsible management keeps the ecological question open.

questions.explanation: 首段明确给出记录到213种鸟类。
questions.evidence_text: recent protection and monitoring recorded 213 bird species.

options: It ends the need for ecological work

questions.explanation: 文章把重新开放视为新测试的开始，并强调持续观察与调整。
questions.evidence_text: Ecologically, however, it is better understood as the start of a new test.

questions.question: What does “baseline” mean in paragraph 3?
options: A starting measure used for comparison

A final judgment on restoration
questions.explanation: 正文逗号后直接解释为用于以后比较的起始测量。
questions.evidence_text: The count of 213 species provides a useful baseline, a starting measure for later comparison.

questions.question: Why are observations needed across seasons?
options: Because bird numbers naturally vary over time
Because visitors arrive only in winter
Because facilities cannot be inspected directly
Because one species count explains every change
questions.explanation: 鸟类并非每月以相同数量出现，因此跨季节记录才能减少对单次数字的误读。
questions.evidence_text: Migratory birds do not appear in the same numbers every month

questions.question: What kind of public access does the author support?

Access that can change in response to evidence
Access without paths or boundaries

questions.evidence_text: It is to design access that can be adjusted when evidence shows stress.

title: The Difficult Middle of a Circular Economy
source_title: China expands circular economy to turn waste into wealth
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开报道；本站选择废旧电缆、厨余处理与二手交易等有限事实，围绕回收链条原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
People often describe a circular economy through its endpoints: an unwanted object goes in, and a useful material comes out. The difficult work lies between them. In Xuzhou, discarded power cables are sorted, dismantled, cleaned, and packed before their copper and aluminum can return to use. A source estimate said that recycling the more than 11,000 tonnes of cable retired by Jiangsu's power sector in 2024 could avoid about 30,000 tonnes of carbon emissions.

A different process is needed for food waste. One industrial park in Suzhou can handle about 500 tonnes of commercial kitchen waste each day. Roughly 90 percent can become soil material, compost, or biogas for the local gas network. These outcomes depend not on calling something “waste,” but on separating inputs and matching each stream with suitable equipment and buyers.

Reuse adds another route. Second-hand platforms circulate appliances, books, digital products, and leisure equipment before recycling is necessary. Yet trust becomes infrastructure in this market. Standard testing, clear prices, and privacy protection can determine whether a used phone changes owners or remains forgotten in a drawer.

The examples show why collection targets alone are incomplete. A pile moved away from households has not necessarily entered a productive cycle. Materials must be identified, processed safely, sold at a usable quality, and accepted by another user or industry. Public participation is essential at the beginning, while standards and markets carry the process through its less visible middle.

Circularity is therefore not a single act of disposal. It is a chain whose environmental value depends on every link continuing to work.

questions.question: What can recovered power cables provide for reuse?
options: Copper and aluminum
Soil and natural gas
Books and instruments
Glass and clean water
questions.explanation: 首段说明废旧电缆经过处理后可回收铜和铝。
questions.evidence_text: their copper and aluminum can return to use.

questions.question: What does the passage emphasize about a circular economy?
options: Its success depends on a functioning chain between collection and reuse
Its only purpose is to increase second-hand prices
All waste should be processed in the same way
Household collection is the final stage
questions.explanation: 文章逐段说明分类、处理、标准、市场等中间环节，并以链条作总结。
questions.evidence_text: It is a chain whose environmental value depends on every link continuing to work.

questions.question: What does “stream” mean in paragraph 2?
options: A category of material moving through a process
A natural river beside the park
A live online video
A payment made to a household
questions.explanation: 语境谈不同投入物的分类和处理，stream 指进入回收流程的一类材料。
questions.evidence_text: matching each stream with suitable equipment and buyers.

questions.question: Why does the author call trust infrastructure in second-hand markets?
options: Because testing, pricing, and privacy rules enable exchanges to occur
Because every used product needs a new road
Because buyers refuse all digital products
Because recycling plants set household prices
questions.explanation: 随后列出的检测、透明定价和隐私保护会决定二手物品能否成交，所以信任像基础设施一样支撑交易。
questions.evidence_text: Standard testing, clear prices, and privacy protection can determine whether a used phone changes owners or remains forgotten in a drawer.

questions.question: How does the author view collection targets?
options: Necessary evidence but insufficient on their own
The only reliable measure of circularity
A barrier to public participation
Less useful than colorful advertising
questions.explanation: 作者明确说仅看收集目标并不完整，材料被移走不等于进入有效循环。
questions.evidence_text: The examples show why collection targets alone are incomplete.

title: The Ten-Second Recycling Moment
source_title: China Focus: From trash to cash -- tech-driven recycling boosts circular economy in China
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开报道；本站选择智能回收箱的操作、规模和后端处理事实，围绕便利与系统能力原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
For a resident, smart recycling can take less than ten seconds: scan a code, open the bin, and put in bottles or boxes. The machine weighs the material and transfers a small payment. In Hangzhou's Xihu District, 870 such units had been placed in nearly 400 communities after a pilot began in July 2024. The reported sorting accuracy reached 98.5 percent, while average monthly collection was about 1,000 tonnes.

Convenience matters because an environmental intention often fails at the moment of effort. If residents must store items for weeks, travel far, or guess which material belongs where, many recyclable objects will enter ordinary rubbish. A nearby machine with an immediate, visible result reduces that friction. The reward is modest, but it confirms that the action was recognized.

Still, the ten-second encounter at the bin is only the front end. Sensors can request collection when a unit is full, and an automated center can divide materials into more than eighty categories before sale. Without pickup schedules, accurate classification, and buyers for the recovered material, a smooth screen would merely hide a growing storage problem.

Technology also changes the evidence available to operators. Usage records can reveal where bins fill quickly and where participation remains low. Yet the same convenience that produces data requires restraint: systems should collect only what is needed for service and payment, explain its use, and offer a practical route for people who do not scan QR codes. Otherwise, a tool designed for broad participation may exclude some residents.

The important innovation is therefore not the smart bin by itself, but the connection between an easy household action and a responsive industrial chain. The public interface deserves praise only when material actually moves onward and the service remains understandable and reachable. Ten seconds may start the cycle; infrastructure completes it.

questions.question: What role do sensors play in the system?
options: They request pickup when a bin becomes full
They set national recycling targets
They repair used furniture
They replace all material buyers
questions.explanation: 第三段直接说明传感器在箱满时触发收运请求。
questions.evidence_text: Sensors can request collection when a unit is full

questions.question: Why can a small immediate reward encourage participation?
options: It confirms the user's action and reduces the sense of effort
It guarantees that every recycling firm is profitable
It makes classification unnecessary
It allows residents to avoid using the bin
questions.explanation: 第二段把即时可见结果与减少行动摩擦联系起来，可推断小额奖励提供确认感。
questions.evidence_text: The reward is modest, but it confirms that the action was recognized.

questions.question: What does “friction” mean in paragraph 2?
options: Practical difficulty that discourages action
Heat produced by moving parts
Disagreement between recycling firms
Damage to a plastic bottle
questions.explanation: 上文列举储存、远行、分类困难，friction 指阻碍行动的现实麻烦。
questions.evidence_text: A nearby machine with an immediate, visible result reduces that friction.

questions.question: Which idea best summarizes the passage?
options: A smart bin works only as part of an accessible collection and processing chain
Recycling succeeds whenever a screen looks simple
Payments are more important than recovered materials
Data collection should have no limits
questions.explanation: 文章从十秒操作转向收运、分类、买方与可达性，核心是前端便利必须连接后端系统。
questions.evidence_text: The important innovation is therefore not the smart bin by itself, but the connection between an easy household action and a responsive industrial chain.

questions.question: How does the author evaluate the public interface?
options: Positively, but only if the full service delivers real and inclusive results
Negatively because digital tools never help
As the only part of recycling worth measuring
As successful whenever it collects personal data
questions.explanation: 末段对界面设置了材料继续流动、服务可理解且可到达的条件。
questions.evidence_text: The public interface deserves praise only when material actually moves onward and the service remains understandable and reachable.

title: A Recycling Target Is a Design Problem
source_title: China to accelerate building of waste-recycling system
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开政策报道；本站保留3R框架及少量目标数字，围绕指标如何塑造系统原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
A national recycling guideline can state an impressive destination, yet the route chosen by its targets will shape what institutions actually build. A 2024 Chinese guideline used the familiar sequence of reducing, reusing, and recycling, while calling for better resource efficiency through precise management and effective recovery. It set 2025 goals that included annual use of four billion tonnes of major solid wastes, a 60-percent utilization rate for newly produced bulk solid waste, and 450 million tonnes of key renewable resources such as scrap metals. It also looked toward a comprehensive and orderly system by 2030.

Numbers are necessary because they turn broad ambition into commitments that can be checked. They can direct investment toward collection networks, processing capacity, and markets for recovered material. Nevertheless, each indicator creates a field of vision: what it counts becomes prominent, while qualities outside the measure can recede. A high utilization volume says little by itself about contamination, energy used in processing, worker safety, or whether recovered material displaces newly extracted resources.

The three-part hierarchy helps clarify this problem. Reduction avoids material demand before waste exists; reuse extends the service of an existing product; recycling processes discarded material into another input. If a policy rewards only tonnes entering recycling plants, institutions may neglect repair systems or packaging changes that prevent waste more effectively. The easiest number to collect can then pull action toward the least preferred stage.

Good implementation therefore requires a dashboard rather than a single total. Volume can be paired with measures of material quality, actual substitution, environmental cost, and access to collection. Categories should also remain visible: success with scrap steel cannot automatically demonstrate success with electronic devices or household food waste, whose hazards and logistics differ.

Targets should guide learning as well as judgment. When a measure rises without the expected environmental benefit, the response should be to inspect the chain and revise incentives, not merely seek a larger number. A recycling system becomes efficient and orderly when its indicators reward the outcome society wants, rather than activity that is easiest to report.

questions.question: Which 2025 goal is mentioned in the passage?
options: Using 450 million tonnes of key renewable resources annually
Ending all production of bulk solid waste
Recycling every electronic device
Replacing the 3R sequence with one target
questions.explanation: 首段列出的目标之一是主要再生资源年利用量达到4.5亿吨。
questions.evidence_text: 450 million tonnes of key renewable resources such as scrap metals.

questions.question: What does the author mean by saying an indicator creates a “field of vision”?
options: It draws attention to counted results while other qualities may be missed
It lets managers see waste from a great distance
It makes every environmental effect measurable
It removes the need to compare categories
questions.explanation: 冒号后的解释说明被计数者会突出，而指标之外的质量可能退居视野之外。
questions.evidence_text: what it counts becomes prominent, while qualities outside the measure can recede.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly arguing?
options: Recycling targets must be designed to reward real environmental outcomes
The largest possible tonnage is always the best policy
Reduction and reuse should be removed from the 3R hierarchy
National guidelines should avoid measurable commitments
questions.explanation: 全文从指标必要性谈到指标偏差，主张多指标并根据实际环境收益修订激励。
questions.evidence_text: A recycling system becomes efficient and orderly when its indicators reward the outcome society wants, rather than activity that is easiest to report.

questions.question: Why might a recycling-only tonnage target weaken waste prevention?
options: It may direct institutions toward processing waste instead of avoiding it
It makes repair easier to measure than recycling
It proves that reused products have no value
It prevents plants from weighing materials
questions.explanation: 若只奖励进入回收厂的吨数，机构可能忽视修理和包装减量，行动会被易统计指标牵引。
questions.evidence_text: If a policy rewards only tonnes entering recycling plants, institutions may neglect repair systems or packaging changes that prevent waste more effectively.

questions.question: What would the author recommend when a measure improves but environmental benefit does not?
options: Examine the chain and change the incentives
Hide the unexpected result
Keep only the rising measure
Assume every category behaves like scrap steel
questions.explanation: 末段明确主张检查链条并修订激励，而不是追求更大的表面数字。
questions.evidence_text: the response should be to inspect the chain and revise incentives, not merely seek a larger number.
